nobox.final_span:
second chapter we read that God got involved, took the hand of Adam and Eve, and made a co-creator of humankind. Scripture indicates that from the start, humans were given a purpose with meaning, and their work held value.
At times, the impact of our work is not enduring. We could generate wealth for our clients or bosses, yet as stated by the prophet Isaiah, our focus should be on contributing to our communities' wealth. Isaiah tells us to strive to be service-oriented people, not those driven by personal ambition. Isaiah 41:17 tells us, “When men plot evil, they plot it for themselves… When I plan an undertaking, I plan it for my people” . Through caring for our brothers and sisters, we care for ourselves. Isaiah speaks about rescuing the prisoners. Once rescued, the prisoners are now citizens of judgment, able to testify to the benefits of our work and its challenges, should another prisoner aspire to follow our path.
As we observe the world, it is apparent that light, love, and joy frequently appear extinguished due to the humorless, unmerciful, and at times violent actions of our sisters and brothers. These observations are not accidental or random occurrences. They occur due to our approach to business, disregarding our role as citizens of creation, which has led to the deepest darkness. Instead of shining a light of love and mercy, we wind up just as disconnected and disinterested as our neighbors. That is not Christian, and it is not beneficial for business.
Train with us, believe in your own power, and step away from the cave! There is work to do and people to aid as the focus shifts from “I” to “we,” showing our trust in God when others waver, and ensuring that we and others are not constrained by expectations or diminished self-regard. At Leo, we guide you to recognize the shells in others, so you can let your light shine upon them, not to highlight their jewelry, but to reveal the presence of the Almighty through your radiant reflection. Our goal is to make lives brighter,
